rows.claim: Epistemic confidence about approval is evidence, never permission: intelligence may rank within the authorized set but cannot convert an unavailable option into a permitted one, even at near-certainty.
rows.quote: Intelligence may optimize within authority; it may not infer authority from optimization.
rows.steal: Before any auto-approve path (workflow yolo bypass, offpeak auto-execution, effect-broker pre-clear), require an explicit grant record naming the consequence class; add the grant-vs-estimate check to the next workflow-gate scenario review of a dispatch shape in configs/workflow_gate_scenarios.
rows.falsifier: A deployed case where acting on 99.9-pct-confidence predicted approval without an explicit class grant repeatedly produced outcomes the principal judged better than asking, with no substitution harm surfacing in audit.

rows.claim: A stored authority record is forensic evidence answering who authorized this and why; it must never imply current permission without revalidation, because authority decays when the intention or circumstances it expressed change.
rows.quote: A stored procedure can carry the former. It must never imply the latter without revalidation.
rows.steal: Audit one standing automation that reuses stored authorization (MagFtsIndexDaily or MagCensusPatrolDaily): confirm its trigger checks current world-state predicates (catalog bytes vs index state, file growth since census date) rather than last-run success, and file the audit row in its log.
rows.falsifier: A class of stored-authority reuse where the authority source and world conditions are provably immutable, so revalidation is redundant in every observed instance and adds cost with zero averted failure.

rows.claim: A decision record a future reader can contest without replaying its context carries at least five elements: the assertion, the evidence available at the time, the authority source, the alternatives considered, and the uncertainty expressed.
rows.quote: If any of these five are missing, a future human cannot distinguish systematic error from acceptable trade-off.
rows.steal: Score the next 5 receipts you write against the five elements (m04.md already carries assertion, evidence, uncertainty via its honesty notes); add explicit alternatives-considered and authority-source lines where missing, starting with this lane's own receipt.
rows.falsifier: A real contested decision successfully revised or revoked by a future reader using a record that lacked one or more of the five elements, with no blind trust required at any step.

rows.claim: Offline continuation under stored authorization verifies observable world-state preconditions of the prior rule; it never predicts the absent human's approval, and silence stays non-authorization.
rows.quote: The system only needs to verify that the observable preconditions of the rule still hold.
rows.steal: Convert one human-judgment guard in a scheduled task into a state predicate with named observable variables (the census patrol's file-growth trigger is the pattern); land in the next revision of scripts/census_patrol_daily.ps1 or log the refusal to convert where no observable predicate exists.
rows.falsifier: An offline-rule execution where correct behavior required estimating the absent human's current preference rather than checking any pre-agreed observable condition, and the state-predicate reading produced the wrong action.

rows.claim: The durable transferable memory unit is not the conclusion or the transcript but the minimum decision ancestry needed to reconstruct why a conclusion deserves to exist: question, competing answers, evidence, contradiction, resolution, open questions.
rows.quote: It may be a decision structure preserving the minimum ancestry necessary to reconstruct why a conclusion deserves to exist.
rows.steal: Extend the next run spec so every lane row carries a falsifier and open-questions field alongside the landed claim (this gala's GalaLaneOut already has falsifier per row); archive question-genealogy, not conclusions only.
rows.falsifier: A memory corpus of bare conclusions with no stored ancestry whose reuse produced no unrecoverable misjudgment across its full lifetime, while an ancestry-carrying twin measurably cost more to store and read.
